lead: Every extra agent reads the context again, spends its own quota, and has to be coordinated. For most code tasks, a single agent, or subagents that return little, gets you more. In this lesson you decide before opening the second agent, using a matrix of signals that runs as a script.
objetivo: decide between a single agent, sequence, parallel, or hybrid using the signal matrix, before opening the second agent.

aprende.t: What a team costs: the published numbers and what they measure
The 6 sequence signals and the 7 parallel ones
The 2-point difference rule and the hybrid
The matrix as a script, with your own tasks

hero_alt: A lone screwdriver on a dark workbench, next to a closed toolbox.

secoes.sub: Click each step. The matrix comes from the arquiteto-de-execucao kit (agenteexecuta).

nos.detalhe: Start with the result and the size. If it fits in one conversation and the done criterion is a single command, there is no team to build.

A simple, small task doesn't go through the matrix: a single agent does it. Opening a subagent to summarize a text is the mistake Anthropic describes in its own research system: agents spawning 50 subagents for simple questions.

itens.t: an early error contaminates the rest

nos.detalhe: One point for each: depends on the previous output; large shared context; decisions need to stay consistent; an early error contaminates several tasks; merging divergent versions is expensive; one step teaches the next.
One point for each: independent tasks; frozen inputs; each output validates on its own; mechanical or deterministic work; small context per task; high urgency; spare machine capacity.

A difference of 2 points or more: the higher side wins. Less than 2, or a tie: hybrid (what depends stays in sequence, the rest in parallel). High cost of error, whatever the score: planning and review stay at the center, even if execution is parallel.

secoes.legenda: The matrix is a starting point, not a measurement. It prevents the reflex of opening agents just because you can.

secoes.titulo: The cost that doesn't show up in the request
secoes.sub: What is published, with dates, and what each number measures.

texto: In Anthropic's post about its research system (06/13/2025): agents use about 4× the tokens of a chat, and multi-agent systems about 15×. The data is theirs, from a research product.
The Claude Code agent teams doc says the same without a number: a team uses significantly more tokens than a single session, and the spend grows with each active teammate.
In the same post, an Opus 4 lead with Sonnet 4 subagents beat Opus 4 alone by 90.2% on their internal research evaluation, on breadth questions (many independent directions).

The post itself warns: most coding tasks have fewer parallelizable parts than research, and agents still coordinate poorly in real time. No measurement from this course shows that gain carrying over to your code.

The arquiteto-de-execucao matrix shows the math (illustrative example, not measured): three agents that read 50k of context and work 20k each add up to 210k; one agent that reuses the context does the same with 110k.
The savings come from not repeating the setup. Parallel pays off when each task has small context.
No subagent without an explicit task, input, and output; at most one level of delegation, unless clearly necessary; two attempts per item before rethinking; don't reprocess an approved item.
Mechanical work (converting, rendering, running tests) goes to a script, not an agent.

secoes.sub: Write each task's signals in a file; the script adds them up and decides. No model involved: it runs for free.

blocos.conteudo:
git clone https://github.com/inematds/inema-agent-runtime.git ~/treino-multi
cd ~/treino-multi && git log -1 --format='%h %cs'   # testado em 5cb431b 2026-10-05

# refactor the login module
S1  each step uses the previous one
S2  the whole module has to be in your head
S3  same names and contracts everywhere
S4  an error in the contract breaks the rest
erro-caro

# convert 500 .md files to .html
P1  one file doesn't depend on another
P2  the converter and the model are locked
P3  each .html checks itself
P4  it's mechanical
P5  each file is small

# market research across 4 segments
S3  the questions have to be the same
S6  the first segment tunes the questions
P1  independent segments
P5  little context per segment

# summarize a text in 5 lines
simples

abas.html:
# refatorar o módulo de login
sequência: 4 · paralelo: 0 · diferença: 4
decisão: sequencial
custo de erro alto: planejamento e revisão centralizados

# converter 500 arquivos .md para .html
sequência: 0 · paralelo: 5 · diferença: 5
decisão: paralelo

# pesquisa de mercado em 4 segmentos
sequência: 2 · paralelo: 2 · diferença: 0
decisão: híbrido

# resumir um texto em 5 linhas
decisão: direto (um agente só, sem matriz)

saída: 0

Converting 500 files is mechanical parallel work: a script with several workers and a sample check at the center (that's lesson 3). The market research came out tied: the first segment runs alone, the other three in parallel.

A lowercase code doesn't count. The script warns you instead of quietly adding it up, and the decision changes. Captured the same day:

# migrar o banco
aviso: código desconhecido 's1' (ignorado)
sequência: 1 · paralelo: 1 · diferença: 0
decisão: híbrido

With the correct S1, it would be sequence 2 × parallel 1, still hybrid, but for a reason you chose. Check grep -c "^aviso:" decisao.md → 0.

secoes.sub: First the example, then three tasks of your own.

exercicios.titulo: E1 · The matrix in the example
exercicios.texto: Clone the practice project, save decide.py and tarefas.txt, and run it.
exercicios.pronto: python3 decide.py tarefas.txt | grep -c "^decisão:" → 4, and the market research comes out as decisão: híbrido.

exercicios.titulo: E2 · Three tasks of your own
exercicios.texto: Write minhas-tarefas.txt with three real tasks from your week (one you've thought about splitting between agents). Mark only the signals that are true today.
exercicios.pronto: python3 decide.py minhas-tarefas.txt > decisao.md; grep -c "^decisão:" decisao.md → 3 and grep -c "^aviso:" decisao.md → 0.

perguntas.p: According to Anthropic's post (Jun/2025), how many tokens does a multi-agent system use compared to a chat?
opcoes: Half, since the work is split
perguntas.explica: About 15× (and single agents, about 4×), in the data from their research system. Splitting the work doesn't split the context: each agent reads its own.

perguntas.p: Sequence 3, parallel 2. What does the matrix say?
perguntas.explica: The difference is 1, less than 2: hybrid. The common mistake is picking the bigger side for any difference at all.

perguntas.p: A migration with a high cost of error scored parallel. What changes?
opcoes: Planning and review stay at the center, even with parallel execution
It only uses the strongest model
perguntas.explica: A costly error centralizes the plan and the review, whatever the score. Running the independent items can still be parallel.

perguntas.p: Why doesn't the research system's 90.2% gain apply directly to your code?
opcoes: Because it was measured on breadth-first research, and code usually has fewer parts that can run in parallel
Because Claude Code has no subagents
perguntas.explica: The post itself makes this caveat: the gain shows up in questions with many independent directions. In code, dependencies weigh more.

itens.texto: Each agent rereads the context and spends its own quota; published: about 15× the tokens of a chat.
Signs of sequence × parallel; a difference of 2 decides, less than that is hybrid; costly errors centralize.
A small task doesn't go through the matrix, and mechanical work goes to a script.
